name: Ice-glazed winter ledge 903
prompt: a chunky rock-face feature made to sit over a cliff wall: a jutting mossy ledge, a thick protruding root knot, or a deep cracked seam in the stone, heavy and solid, ice-glazed winter ledge, roughly six feet tall, human height, completely unlit, no glow, no light sources, no self-emission

placement.note: ONE SCENERY PIXEL IS ONE PLAYER PIXEL. world_px_height IS the art's own alpha bbox height, so scenery is placed into the world at 1:1 exactly as the avatar is (setScale(1)) and the two share one pixel grid. The CAMERA still zooms the whole scene — that is uniform and correct; what must never happen is scenery being resampled on its own, against the player. world_height_m is what the art reads as beside a 87px character; declared_height_m is what it was once declared to be, and a gap between them means the ART is the wrong size.

renamed_why: crash-window re-roll squatted a judged id; fresh id so old verdicts point at nothing and this enters the review queue as the new piece it is

LIT_1.glow_concept: warm light spilling from a deep crevice

motion.description: This is the same picture in every frame. ONLY the gold seam through the rock brightens a little and returns. It is lit and clearly visible in every frame, including the first. It gets only SLIGHTLY brighter -- never white, never washed out -- and keeps its own colour throughout: brightest in the middle, back to its first-frame brightness at the end, never dimmer at the end than the start. Nothing is added or removed anywhere: every object appears in every frame, the same number of them, in the same places, at the same size. Everything else is copied from the first frame exactly, pixel for pixel: same shape, size, position and colour, no outline redrawn. The last frame matches the first exactly.

This is the same picture in every frame. ONLY the green light on the crystals brightens a little and returns. It is lit and clearly visible in every frame, including the first. It gets only SLIGHTLY brighter -- never white, never washed out -- and keeps its own colour throughout: brightest in the middle, back to its first-frame brightness at the end, never dimmer at the end than the start. The things carrying it keep exactly the shape, size, position and number they have in the first frame. Everything else is copied from the first frame exactly, pixel for pixel: same shape, size, position and colour, no outline redrawn. The last frame matches the first exactly.

light.reference: the spawn bonfire is 1.0 (radius 7); strength 0 is no light
